ai.title: Add /dashboard slash command and account hub usage types
ai.summary: A new `/dashboard` slash command opens `${LOGIN_WEBSITE_URL}/account` via `safeOpen` and prints a system message announcing streaks, activity, tokens, sessions and settings across CLI, Desktop and web; it is Freebuff-only (registered in `FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMANDS`), while Codebuff keeps its separate `/usage` banner. The dashboard reuses the `usage` alias because Freebuff removes the old `/usage` command, leaving users without an answer to how much they have used. Two new files wire the account hub: `common/src/types/freebuff-usage.ts` adds the cross-surface summary interfaces, and `common/src/util/freebuff-usage-summary.ts` adds pure functions `buildFreebuffUsageSummary`, `calculateLongestFreebuffStreak`, and `buildFreebuffUsageGrid`, driven by new constants `FREEBUFF_USAGE_MAP_DAYS = 365` and `FREEBUFF_RECENT_TOKENS_DAYS = 7` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`.

facts: The form is required: no skip, every question answered. That creates a trap we have to design against, if saving is broken on our side, a required form plus a redirect that fires until it is answered is an infinite loop into a screen the user cannot get past however hard they try.
So this cookie is set ONLY after a save attempt fails, never on arrival and never by a user choosing to leave. A working system is not skippable; a broken one does not hold anyone hostage.

ai.summary: Renamed ONBOARDING_SEEN_COOKIE to ONBOARDING_BYPASS_COOKIE in freebuff-onboarding-gate.ts. The bypass cookie now sets only after save failures, not on arrival, preventing infinite redirect loops during outages. TTL reduced from 180 days to 24 hours in common/src/constants. eli5.text: You will no longer get stuck on the sign-up questions page if the system fails to save your answers. Because the questions are required and can't be skipped, a broken save used to trap you in an endless loop on that screen. Now the system lets you past the page only after a save attempt has actually failed, and that temporary pass expires in a day. The form now also tells you to pick an option for any question you leave blank. This is live now and only affects sign-up flows.

ai.title: Document global-jsdom load-order flake and restore rules
ai.summary: Added section detailing file-order dependency in `test-freebuff-desktop` caused by `global-jsdom` caching `KEYS` at module scope. Explains how leaked `requestAnimationFrame` stubs in earlier suites poisoned subsequent React tests, leading to cascading failures. Defines two rules: delete global keys when restoring (not assign `undefined`) and use `test/support/jsdom.ts` for isolated DOM globals.

eli5.text: Intermittent React rendering test failures across approximately twenty unrelated component tests (Tab.rename, ContextBar.menu, AccountMenu.menu, AgentPicker.menu, QuotaBadge) occurred when an earlier test file left a fake "requestAnimationFrame" function on the shared test environment that never actually triggered callbacks. The documentation now records why this happened: the shared DOM setup tool captures which browser functions exist the first time it runs and reuses that list for every test, so a leftover stub from one test file caused five subsequent files to hang waiting for animation frames that never fired. To prevent recurrence, the fix requires properly removing any fake browser functions during test cleanup rather than just blanking them, and always obtaining the shared DOM

The picker used to show the fast-but-limited basic model first, then the deeper-reasoning premium model second; the project flipped its recommended default to the premium model on August 12, but the on-screen order never caught up until now. eli5.text: You, as a user, can now rest easy knowing that the list of recommended AI models shown to you will stay in the right order even if the company later changes which model is set as the default. The engineering team added a behind-the-scenes checklist (a test) that automatically checks if the first model in the list is still the one meant to be the default, and the second is still the designated runner-up. If it ever isn’t, the system will flag it before it goes live, preventing the list you see from accidentally showing the wrong order.
